rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly life spent without seeking the hereafter is a fleeting life that deceives and exhausts, with no lasting fruit.
rows.anchor: Dünyâ hayat yani âhiret kazancı için sarfedilmeyen, âlem-i bekā nimetlerinin iktisâbına vâsıta kılınmayan fâni hayat

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Play absorbs effort but ends in nothing whether one wins or loses.
rows.anchor: Yense de yenilse de netice itibariyle hiçe müncer olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Diversion keeps people from useful work, duty, and livelihood, and merely wastes time.
rows.anchor: insanı fâideli olan işinden, gücünden, vazifesinden alıkoyan ve vaktini öldürmekten başka bir işe yaramayan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adornment is outward display, confers no intrinsic honor, and deceives the heedless through clothes and finery.
rows.anchor: zâtî bir şeref bahşetmeyen ve kadınlar, çocuklar gibi gāfilleri aldatan giyimler kuşanımlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mutual boasting means competing in pride, claiming superiority through external things such as lineage; pride relies on things outside oneself.
rows.anchor: “ben senden üstünüm, ben fülan oğluyum” gibi bir övünüş, bir kurum. “Tefâhur” iftihar yarışı etmektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People compete to accumulate wealth and children as a source of pride.
rows.anchor: Ve emvâl ü evlâdda bir çokluk yarışı, bir gurur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who live solely for the world make all their efforts serve these distractions and contests.
rows.anchor: İşte sırf dünya için yaşayanlara hayat bunlardan ibarettir. Onların bütün mesâîleri bunlar içindir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Kuffār” can mean unbelievers in its familiar religious sense, but Elmalılı prefers Ibn Masʿūd’s reported sense of farmers, from the root meaning to cover seed with soil; the wording also alludes to unbelievers’ animal life.
rows.anchor: İbn Mes‘ûd radıyallâhu anh Hazretleri’nden mervî olduğu üzere çiftçi rençberler mânasına olması daha müreccahtır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The crop first delights the farmers, then matures, yellows, and becomes dry chaff, illustrating worldly life’s decline.
rows.anchor: Sonra heyecâna gelir coşar, gürelir, yahut kurumaya yüz tutar, körelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife offers severe punishment for absorption in worldly life, but also divine forgiveness that covers sins and erases hardship.
rows.anchor: dünyâ hayâta inhimâkin neticesi olan elîm bir acıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine pleasure is greater than every pleasure: the believer is both accepted by God and content with Him, an enduring perfection of joy.
rows.anchor: hem marzî hem râzı olmak, o ebedî hoşnutluk, bütün saadetlerin a‘zamı, bütün safâların ekmelidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgiveness and divine pleasure are promised to believers who do not make worldly life their goal and instead work for the hereafter.
rows.anchor: dünyâ hayâtı gaye edinmeyip âhiret için çalışan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning forgiveness and divine pleasure alongside punishment signals that mercy predominates.
rows.anchor: şedîd bir azâba mukabil iki şey zikrolunuyor: mağfiret ve rıdvan; bunda rahmetin galebesine bir tenbih vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly life is a deceptive provision: it seems pleasant but ends in grief, pain, and punishment.
rows.anchor: Bir metâ‘dır fakat bir aldanma metâ‘ıdır. Hoş gibi görünür lâkin neş’esi humar ile, zevki elem ü hicran

rows.speaker: Sa‘îd b. Cübeyr
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr explains that worldly provision is deceptive because it distracts people from seeking the hereafter.
rows.anchor: metâ‘-ı gurûr olması, âhiret talebinden alıkoyması cihetiyledir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly goods become excellent provision when used as a means to seek God’s pleasure and the goods of the hereafter.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ’nın rıdvânına ve âhiret metâlibine vesile edinilmesi haysiyetiyle ne güzel metâ‘, ne güzel vesiledir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should not be carried away by temporary pleasures; they should work for the hereafter from love of forgiveness and divine pleasure as well as fear of punishment.
rows.anchor: yalnız azab korkusuyla değil o mağfiret ve rıdvâna lâyık bir neş’e, bir aşk u mahabbet ile âhiret için çalışmalı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Racing and hastening are not identical in meaning, but both involve speed and striving to overtake others.
rows.anchor: “Müsâra‘at” ve “müsâbaka” sür‘at yarışı, geçmek yarışı, mefhûmen farklı olmakla beraber mütelâzimdirler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should compete like runners in good works, surpass earlier communities, and prepare what is needed to reach forgiveness and the garden.
rows.anchor: sizden evvelki ümmetlerin sâbikūnunu geçmek ve onlardan daha ileri olarak Rabbinizin mağfiretine ve tavsif olunan cennet ü rıdvâna ermek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden is prepared for those who believe in God and His messengers; the real competition begins with faith and the greatest possible effort to affirm and practice revelation.
rows.anchor: O hâlde müsâbakanın aslını bu imanda müsâbaka teşkil eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden is God’s gracious gift, not something owed to people; He grants His favor to whom He wills.
rows.anchor: Üzerine vâcib olduğu için değil, mahza fazl u keremiyle ihsan ettiği bir atıyyesi, bir bahşişidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should strive in faith and hope for success through God’s immense favor.
rows.anchor: muvaffakiyeti yine O’nun fazlından ümid edin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earthly and personal calamities are written in advance; a calamity is an event that strikes a person severely.
rows.anchor: “Musîbet” hedefine isabet eden mermi gibi insana

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earthly calamities include drought, famine, damage to crops or livestock, destruction of homes or cities, earthquakes, and other losses; personal ones include death, illness, injury, imprisonment, hunger, thirst, and poverty.
rows.anchor: Kuraklık, kıtlık hâsılat veya hayvânâta ârız olan âfetler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God recorded calamities in His eternal knowledge or the Preserved Tablet before creating the earth, people, or the calamities themselves.
rows.anchor: Tatlı muvaffakiyetler Allah’ın fazlı olduğu gibi bütün musibetler de Allah’ın ilm-i ezelîsinde veya Levh-i Mahfuz’da yazılmış bir takdîridir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This prior writing is easy for God, who is independent of matter and time.
rows.anchor: Çünkü Allah teâlâ madde ve müddetten müstağnîdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People cannot escape a decreed calamity: it reaches those who flee or sit back in comfort as well as those who strive.
rows.anchor: mukadder olan musibetten ise kaçınmakla kurtulunmaz. O yazılmış ise yalnız müsâbakaya girişenlere değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Belief in divine decree gives the heart strength and steadiness through painful and pleasant events.
rows.anchor: kalbe kuvvet ve metanet vermek, gerek acı ve gerek tatlı hâdisât karşısında sarsılmamak için büyük fâideleri

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calamities are recorded so people do not despair over what they lose or become proud of what they receive; Solomon’s response models seeing gifts as a test.
rows.anchor: “Allah’ın takdîri böyle imiş” diye mütesellî olup metanetinizi muhafaza edesiniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A believer may naturally feel sorrow or happiness, but should not be swept into despair or pride; seeing hidden wisdom in events, one keeps to duty with trust and contentment.
rows.anchor: hasbe’l-beşeriye müteessir veya mütehassis olsa da kendini şaşırmaz, ne gamın ıztırâbına ne de sevincin gurur ve heyecânına kaptırmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not love the conceited boaster; the blameworthy kind of joy is excessive confidence that brings pride.
rows.anchor: Demek ki mezmum olan ferah kibir ve gurur getiren fazla güveniştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Muhtāl” describes an arrogant person who imagines a virtue in himself; “fakhūr” is an intensive form meaning one who boasts greatly.
rows.anchor: “fehûr” mübalağa sîgasıdır. Çok iftihar edici demektir. “Muhtâl” de “ihtiyâl”den ism-i fâil olup

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “lilladhīna” grammatically either substitutes for “muhtāl” or predicates an omitted subject meaning “they are those”; it cannot be an adjective because it is definite while “muhtāl” is indefinite.
rows.anchor: sıfat olamaz. Çünkü مُخْتَالٍۢ nekre

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conceited hoard wealth, refuse charity and aid or spending in God’s path, and encourage others to be stingy by advice or by example.
rows.anchor: Sadaka ve i‘âne vermekten, Allah yolunda infak eylemekten mallarını kıskanır, esirgerler, hasislik ederler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning away means refusing to spend in God’s path; God is self-sufficient and worthy of praise, so the loss belongs only to those who withhold.
rows.anchor: Onların yüz çevirmeleriyle O’nun hiçbir şeyi eksilmez, zarar onların kendilerine ait olur

rows.speaker: نافع، ابن عامر، أبو جعفر
rows.claim: These readers recite the passage without the quoted waw phrase; the meaning remains unchanged.
rows.anchor: Nâfi‘, İbn Âmir, Ebû Ca‘fer kıraatlerinde وَلَهْوٌۭ’siz فَاِنَّ اللهَّٰ الْغَنِيُّ الْحَم۪يدُ okunur. Mâna değişmez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent messengers with clear, decisive proofs and miracles, and revealed the book and the scale with them.
rows.anchor: açık ve kat‘î burhanlar ve mucizelerle resullerimizi gönderdik

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The book” is generic and includes teaching people writing; the scale is a familiar balance used as a sign and standard of equilibrium, taught to humanity by God and tied to rational judgment.
rows.anchor: “Kitâb”dan murad cinstir. Yazının bildirilmesi de zımnındadır. “Mîzân” da mâlum terazi demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book and scale were given so people would stand upright in fairness and justice.
rows.anchor: ki nâs insaf ve adaletle doğrulsun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A physical scale cannot measure every legal balance, so “scale” here appropriately symbolizes the standard of justice for legal, social, and political relations.
rows.anchor: “mîzân” hukūkī, ictimâ‘î, siyasî muvâzeneyi tâyin eden mi‘yâr-ı adalet mânasına olmak münâsibdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made iron abundant and taught people how to use it; it brings severe force through steel weapons and also many benefits.
rows.anchor: Bir de demiri indirdik yani mebzûlen yaratıp mevcûdiyetini bildirdik, kullanılmasını öğrettik

rows.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
rows.claim: Razi says iron benefits humanity far more than gold: without gold worldly affairs would lose little, but without iron nearly all would be disrupted.
rows.anchor: Fahreddin Râzî’nin dediği gibi demirin insanlığa

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iron is the backbone and working hand of industry and civilization, serving nearly every craft and everyday need.
rows.anchor: İğneden ipliğe hiçbir sanat yoktur ki onda demirin hizmet ve menfaati olmasın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Modern machinery has greatly increased both iron’s destructive force and its benefits; iron-bound oppression and explosives show its severity, while aircraft show its immense uses.
rows.anchor: Hem be’s-i şedîdi artırmış, hem menâfi‘i çoğaltmıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iron is more available than gold because humanity needs it more; gold is scarce and buried deep, making it a durable measure of value.
rows.anchor: demiri altından çok ve kolay bulunur bir surette yaratmış ve altından önce keşfini müyesser de kılmıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s wisdom makes things more plentiful and accessible as need for them increases: air is easiest to obtain, then water, then food, while gems are rare because they are less needed.
rows.anchor: tab‘an bir şeye ihtiyaç ne kadar çoksa o da hilkatte o nisbette çok bulunur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because humanity needs God’s mercy more than anything else, Elmalılı hopes and prays that God makes it the easiest grace to find.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ’nın bize rahmetini her şeyin en kolay bulunan bir fazlı kılacağını da ümid ve niyaz ederiz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı links this passage’s book and scale to verses about God’s revealed book and the balance raised in creation.
rows.anchor: وَٱلسَّمَآءَ رَفَعَهَا وَوَضَعَ ٱلْمِيزَانَ

rows.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
rows.claim: Razi’s first analogy: the book guides right inward knowledge and action, the scale guides bodily dealings and distinguishes justice from injustice, and iron force restrains wrongdoing; this order ranks spiritual, bodily, then coercive concerns.
rows.anchor: Fahreddin Râzî tefsirindeki şu güzel vecihleri okumadan geçmeyelim: “1. Teklîfin medârı iki emirdir: Birisi lâyık olanı yapmak, ikincisi de lâyık olmayanı terketmektir

rows.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
rows.claim: Razi’s second analogy: dealings with the Creator proceed through the book, dealings with friends through equality and the scale, and dealings with enemies through the sword and iron.
rows.anchor: Muamele ya Hâlık iledir, bunun yolu kitaptır

rows.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
rows.claim: Razi’s third analogy divides people into forerunners, moderates, and wrongdoers: forerunners treat others by the book and show leniency to themselves, moderates need the scale, and oppressors need iron.
rows.anchor: İnsanlar üç kısımdır. Birincisi sâbikūndur. Onlar halka kitabın muktezâsına göre muamele ederler

rows.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
rows.claim: Razi’s fourth analogy maps the book to the station of truth and the settled soul, the scale to the ethical path of moderation, and iron to the difficult discipline of the commanding self; he cites 13:28.
rows.anchor: nefs-i mutmainne ve mukarrebîn makamıdır

rows.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
rows.claim: Razi’s fifth analogy assigns the book to those who attain direct unveiling, the scale to seekers who need evidence, and iron to the removal of stubborn disputants.
rows.anchor: İnsan ya mükâşefe sâhibi vâsılîndendir. Onun enîsi ancak kitap ve zikrullahtır

rows.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
rows.claim: Razi’s sixth analogy says the book supplies religious fundamentals, the scale establishes justice in practical rulings, and iron disciplines those who abandon both paths.
rows.anchor: Din ya usûl veya fürû‘dur. Diğer bir tâbir ile ya ma‘ârif veya a‘mâl ve ahlâktır

rows.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
rows.claim: Razi’s seventh analogy makes the book the source of just rulings, the scale the government’s implementation of justice, and iron the force used against rebels; this places scholars above rulers.
rows.anchor: Kitap, Allah teâlâ’nın kitâbında zikreylediği adl ü insâfı muktezî ahkâma işarettir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The book, scale, and iron teach reading and justice, encourage adherence to truth, warn against force, and let people benefit from iron in government, industry, and trade.
rows.anchor: nâs okumayı ve adalet ölçülerini bellesin, adl ü hakka niyetle tutunsun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God distinguishes and rewards those who support Him and His messengers sincerely, without show, before they reach His presence; helping God means helping the religion and expending one’s own will.
rows.anchor: Allah kendisine ve gönderdiği peygamberlerine ani’l-gıyâb

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Helping God” means supporting the religion and using one’s free will, as also indicated in 47:7.
rows.anchor: irâde-i cüz’iyeyi sarftır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is strong and mighty, fully able to do whatever He wills and never defeated; the call to help benefits people rather than meeting any divine need.
rows.anchor: Şüphe yok ki Allah Kavî’dir, Azîz’dir. Kuvveti pek çok, izzetine nihâyet yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing assurance confirms the truth, removes the imagined notion that God needs help, shows that the benefit of striving belongs to people, and warns against disobedience.
rows.anchor: nusret ve mücahede tekliflerinin fâidesi insanların kendilerine ait olduğunu ihtar ve aynı zamanda muhalefetten tahzir için beliğ bir inzardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers must seek God’s protection from hypocrisy, disbelief, injustice, and the evil end brought by Satan, obeying His commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: Hep Allah’a korunun nifaktan, münafıklardan, küfürden, kâfirlerden, zulümden, zâlimlerden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each person should examine what they have sent ahead for the Day of Resurrection and take account of themselves before being called to account.
rows.anchor: her nefis yarın için, yani gelecek kıyamet günü için ne hazırlamış, Allah’a ne takdim eylemiş olduğuna nazar etsin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation calls the Judgment Day “tomorrow” to make it feel as near as tomorrow and spur preparation.
rows.anchor: Yarın dünden yakın olmak itibariyle yarın olacakmış gibi yakın telakkī edilerek çalışılmasına tenbihtir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation sees earthly life and the hereafter as two divine days: this world is today and the afterlife tomorrow.
rows.anchor: bugün dünya yarın âhiret demek olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse also urges people each day to consider what they have done for the coming day.
rows.anchor: insanın dünyada ömründen her gün korunmak için yarına yarar ne yaptığını düşünmesi lüzûmunu ihtardan da hâlî değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated command to fear God is not redundant: the first stresses loving obedience and fulfilling duties, while the second stresses fearing and avoiding forbidden acts.
rows.anchor: evvelki Allah sevgisiyle emirlerin, vazifelerin îfâsı, bu da Allah korkusuyla menhiyyâttan, fenalıklardan sakınılması siyâkında olmak itibariyle farklıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows all deeds and will accordingly recompense people with punishment or reward.
rows.anchor: Allah her ne yaparsanız şüphesiz habîrdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is to sincere believers seeking the divine honor granted to believers.
rows.anchor: Allah’a ve Resûlüne hâlisâne iman etmiş olup da Allah yanında mü’minlere mahsus bulunan ilâhî izzete ermek isteyen mü’minler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cares of wealth and children must not distract believers from remembering God; the verse does not command abandoning these responsibilities.
rows.anchor: “Zikrullah” Allah düşüncesi, Allah anımı ki müfessirînin beyânına göre

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “God’s remembrance” includes prayer and other obligatory and voluntary worship that recalls God’s names, attributes, commands, reward, and punishment and trains people to act for Him.
rows.anchor: burada murad Allah’ı zikr ü ta‘zîm için yapılan namaz gibi ibadetlerle onun semeresi olarak Allah mahabbetiyle yapılan ubûdiyetlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worship includes congregational prayer, fasting, almsgiving, pilgrimage, struggle, Qur’an recitation, preaching, and acts of glorification and praise.
rows.anchor: namaz, oruç, zekât, hac, cihad, kırâat-i Kur’an, va‘z u nasihat, tehlil, tesbih, tahmid

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever lets wealth and children cause forgetfulness of God is a loser who traded the everlasting for the fleeting and loses lasting honor.
rows.anchor: Çok ziyan etmiş, bâkīyi fânîye değişmiş, sonunda bâkiyât izzetinden mahrum kalmış kimselerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı links the warning to the verse that calls wealth and children worldly adornment and lasting good deeds better with God.
rows.anchor: Çünkü ٱلْمَالُ وَٱلْبَنُونَ زِينَةُ ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَٱلْبَٰقِيَٰتُ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتُ خَيْرٌ عِندَ رَبِّكَ ثَوَابًۭا وَخَيْرٌ أَمَلًۭا’dır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spending from what God has provided is the second trait, alongside remembrance of God, by which believers attain honor and prepare for the resurrection and Day of Mutual Loss.
rows.anchor: iki haslet gösteriliyor. Birisi zikrullahtan gaflet etmemek, birisi de infak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report transmitted by Tirmidhi and others says the assembly of the highest angels debates two matters: expiations and degrees.
rows.anchor: en yüksek cemiyet olan melâikenin bütün münakaşaları iki şey üzerinedir. Birisi keffârât, birisi de derecâttır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report lists expiations as walking to good deeds or congregational prayer, remaining in mosques after prayers, and performing ablution well in hardship.
rows.anchor: namazlardan sonra mescidlerde cülûs, kerih hâllerden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report lists elevated degrees as feeding people, spreading peace, and praying at night while others sleep.
rows.anchor: İt‘âm-ı ta‘âm, neşr-i selâm, herkes uyurken salâta kıyâm

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: The Prophet’s supplication asks for good deeds, avoidance of wrong, love of the poor, forgiveness and mercy, protection from a people’s trial, and love of God, His beloved, and deeds that draw near to Him.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah buyurmuştur ki: “Bu haktır, bunu ders edin belleyin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All good deeds are done from love of God; some expiate sins and others raise rank, with feeding the needy, spreading peace, and night prayer leading the latter.
rows.anchor: Demek ki bütün güzel ameller Allah sevgisiyle yapılan işlerdir. Ve bunların bir kısmı keffârât, bir kısmı da derecâttır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer heads both the expiations and the degrees, but without almsgiving people cannot rise to the honor God bestows.
rows.anchor: Allah hem evvel hem âhir olduğu için demek ki zikrullâhın en mühimi olan namaz da hem keffârâtın başında hem derecâtın müntehâsındadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling zakat the bridge of Islam means it is a passage to higher degrees; after obligatory dues, voluntary charity and assistance bring the greatest nearness to God.
rows.anchor: derecâta yükselmek için köprü ve geçit mesabesinde olduğunu anlatmaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should not only tend to wealth and family but should earn, spend in God’s path, and strive to reach a higher rank before death.
rows.anchor: ölmezden evvel efendilik derecesine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True honor lies in feeding others; people who gorge themselves but withhold spending and ignore nearby needy people are merely losers.
rows.anchor: asıl izzet yemekte değil, yedirmektedir. Kendileri patlayasıya yiyip de Allah için yedirmekten, vergi vermekten kaçınan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı says such selfishness leads to the collapse of barriers and allows Gog and Magog to devastate the land.
rows.anchor: Böylelerin yüzündendir ki sedler yıkılır, Ye’cûc ve Me’cûc arzı tahrip eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He identifies refusal to spend as the root of modern communism and fascism conflicts; lower societies fight over eating others’ earnings, by force, theft, or begging.
rows.anchor: dünyada cem‘iyyet-i beşeriyeyi en ziyade yoran

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Higher societies compete in feeding, giving, completing others’ needs, covering faults, and reaching divine ranks through service.
rows.anchor: yedirmek, infak etmek ve muhtaç olanların ihtiyaçlarına yetişerek Allah’a kullukta yükselmek yarışı üzerinde dolaşır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels’ highest assembly contends over expiations and degrees, while the ongoing cleansing, healing, and provision of creation reflects their work under divine commands.
rows.anchor: Hilkatte mütemadiyen pisliklerin temizlenip durması, yaraların iyileşmesi, havâyic ve erzâkın en hurde uzviyetlere kadar yetiştirilip tevzî‘olunması

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islam raises believers to angelic honor through remembrance of God and spending; acquiring wealth for this purpose is nobler than earning only for family concerns.
rows.anchor: mütevakkıf olduğu esbâbın kesbi ile de emirdir. Ve bu maksadla kesb yalnız evlâd u iyâl endişesiyle kesbden çok yüksek bir himmettir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers with this aspiration avoid the humiliation of begging unless severely compelled, like the poor described in 2:273.
rows.anchor: pek ziyade muztar olmadıkça tese’’ül zilletini irtikâbdan elbette uzaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earning and managing wealth or family is not forbidden; what is forbidden is forgetting God and failing to consider spending for Him.
rows.anchor: menhî olan mal kazanmak ve mal ve evlâd tedbir ve terbiyesiyle müstefid olmak değil, mal ve evlâd endişesiyle Allah’ı unutmak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should regard their wealth as God’s provision rather than the fruit of their own ability, and therefore willingly sacrifice in His path.
rows.anchor: malı da sırf kendinin ve kendi marifet ve iktidârının semeresi bilmeyip Allah’ın kendine merzuk kıldığı bir atıyye-i ilâhiye telakkī etmesi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dying person who failed to give will beg for a brief extension so they can give charity and become righteous, then grieve over leaving without those blessings.
rows.anchor: yâ Rab! Ne olur beni yakın bir ecele kadar tehir etsen

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should spend from their provision before death, because when the appointed term arrives God will not delay a soul, and later remorse will be useless.
rows.anchor: Allah bir nefsi eceli geldiği vakit de asla tehir etmez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows every deed, rewarding those who remember and spend for Him and punishing those who forget Him and plunge into worldly life.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın zikrinden gaflet etmeyip Allah için infak edenlerin de yaptıklarını bilir, mükâfatlarını verir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This profit and loss becomes clear on the Day of Account and Mutual Loss, and the chapter is followed by Sūrat al-Taghābun.
rows.anchor: Bu da kâr ve zarar günü olan hesab ve tegābün günü belli olacaktır. Onun için bu sûreyi de Sûre-i Tegābün tâkip edecektir
